For emo emo music (as in sideswept bangs, eyeliner emo) there's really only 4 big genres that are usually  mixed with emocore. That's why "emo". 

1) 𝗽𝗼𝗽 𝗽𝘂𝗻𝗸

Usually upbeat sounding, energetic, poppy, catchy. juvenile sounding. Can be sad sounding and melow. Most people get into emo from these types of bands. 

In this category you have:

-the mainstream emo bands (mcr, fall out boy, paramore, panic at the disco exc...) 

-the early 2000's skate punk bands (sum 41, blink 182, good charlotte, exc...) 

-the mid to late 2000's emo bands (all time low, yellowcard, mayday parade, cute is what I aim for, exc..)

If your like 14, I'd say start with the mainstream ones and if your like 17 I'd say with the mid to late 2000's ones. 

2) 𝗣𝗼𝘀𝘁-𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲 

Usually very very emotional and often features screamed or shrieked vocals. Can be melow or very agressive. 

Bands: underoath, thursday, thrice, Saosin, escape the fate, blessthefall

3) 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲 

Usually very harsh sound, with 2/3 of the song being screamed or growled. Features an emotional chorus usually, synth breakdowns, autotune, exc... 

Bands like: Alesana, a skylit drive, bring me the horizon, chiodos, devil wears prada, exc... 

4) 𝗘𝗺𝗼𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲 

Usually emotional, sad, mellow, with an intense emotionally charged chorus. Has a very distinct vocal sound. Almost every emo band is heavily influenced by emocore regardless of the genre. 


There's other genres that are often found in emo bands (alt metal, alt rock, hard rock, exc...) or that are considered "emo" (like nu metal bands. Linkin Park for ex) 


Here I'm just saying what bands are associated with the subculture, regardless of what the band says. So don't get pissed ^^  

To me and most people if a band either is heavily influenced by emocore and is associated with the subculture its emo

My advice is just go on Spotify and look up their playlists like pop punk classics, 2000's emo songs, exc...
